metadata.question: Did New York experience an air temperature difference of at least 24 degrees Celcius between January 29 and February 5, 2019?

data.raw_code: 1. Search strategy: - Location: New York State (approximately center at ~43.3°N, -75.7°W, or use a bounding box) - Dates: January 29, 2019 and February 5, 2019 - Data source: ERA5 or MODIS Land Surface Temperature (LST). ERA5 provides 2m air temperature, which is more appropriate than LST. - Collection: `ECMWF/COPERNICUS/ERA5/MONTHLY` or `ECMWF/COPERNICUS/ERA5/DAILY` for daily air temperature. 2. Masking strategy: - No cloud masking needed; ERA5 is a reanalysis product (gridded data without clouds). - Simply filter by date and location, then extract 2m air temperature. 3. Logic to distinguish Valid Zero (A/B) from Null/Error (C3): - Fetch mean air temperature for Jan 29, 2019 and Feb 5, 2019. - Calculate the absolute difference. - If either date has no valid data, output C1. - If difference is a valid number and >= 24°C, output A; else B. - If result is None/NaN or out of reasonable range (e.g., < -50°C or > 60°C for NY), output C3. ```javascript const ee = require('@google/earthengine'); const privateKey = require('../auth_keys/test-project-473922-29f05d49bed7'); async function runAnalysis() { // Define New York region (bounding box) const nyGeometry = ee.Geometry.Rectangle([-79.5, 40.5, -71.5, 45.0]); // ERA5 daily air temperature const era5Daily = ee.ImageCollection('ECMWF/COPERNICUS/ERA5/DAILY'); // Filter for Jan 29, 2019 const jan29 = era5Daily .filterDate('2019-01-29', '2019-01-30') .filterBounds(nyGeometry) .select('temperature_2m'); // Filter for Feb 5, 2019 const feb5 = era5Daily .filterDate('2019-02-05', '2019-02-06') .filterBounds(nyGeometry) .select('temperature_2m'); const size29 = jan29.size().getInfo(); const size5 = feb5.size().getInfo(); console.log(`Jan 29 Images: ${size29}, Feb 5 Images: ${size5}`); // Check if data exists if (size29 === 0 || size5 === 0) { console.log("No data available for one or both dates."); console.log("C1"); return; } // Get mean temperature for each date (convert from Kelvin to Celsius) const temp29Img = jan29.mean(); const temp5Img = feb5.mean(); const temp29K = temp29Img.reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.mean(), geometry: nyGeometry, scale: 10000, maxPixels: 1e9 }).get('temperature_2m').getInfo(); const temp5K = temp5Img.reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.mean(), geometry: nyGeometry, scale: 10000, maxPixels: 1e9 }).get('temperature_2m').getInfo(); // Convert from Kelvin to Celsius const temp29C = temp29K - 273.15; const temp5C = temp5K - 273.15; console.log(`Jan 29 Temp: ${temp29C.toFixed(2)}°C, Feb 5 Temp: ${temp5C.toFixed(2)}°C`); // Validate results if (temp29C === null || temp5C === null || isNaN(temp29C) || isNaN(temp5C)) { console.log("Calculation resulted in null or NaN."); console.log("C3"); return; } // Check if temperatures are within reasonable range for NY if (temp29C < -50 || temp29C > 50 || temp5C < -50 || temp5C > 50) { console.log("Temperature out of reasonable range for New York."); console.log("C3"); return; } // Calculate absolute difference const tempDiff = Math.abs(temp29C - temp5C); console.log(`Temperature Difference: ${tempDiff.toFixed(2)}°C`); // Check if difference >= 24°C if (tempDiff >= 24.0) { console.log("A"); } else { console.log("B"); } } async function initEE() { await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.data.authenticateViaPrivateKey(privateKey, resolve, reject); }); await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.initialize(null, null, resolve, reject); }); await runAnalysis(); } initEE(); ```
